ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image a central carbon can be seen, connected to the right to an ester carbonyl fragment C(=O)OR¹, connected to the left to an acyl fragment R-C(=O), also connected to H, and connected upward to a diazosulfonyl group N=N-N(-)-SO2Tol; the curved arrows in the figure indicate electron transfer and are ignored according to the question. Replace both variables R and R¹ with wildcard symbols *. From the right-side ester fragment, write *OC(=O)-, attached to the central carbon; add the branch /N=N\[N-]S(=O)(=O)c1cccc(C)c1 on the central carbon to represent the N=N-N(-)-SO2Tol in the figure; finally attach the left-side acyl C(*)=O. Therefore the SMILES obtained is *OC(=O)C(/N=N\[N-]S(=O)(=O)c1cccc(C)c1)C(*)=O.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a central carbon connected to two carbonyl substituents, H, and an N=N-N(-)-SO2Tol group, while explicitly discarding the curved arrows. Then build the SMILES from the right ester R1O-C(=O)- fragment, attach the central carbon, add the diazo sulfonyl branch with `[N-]S(=O)(=O)c1cccc(C)c1`, and finish with the left acyl R carbonyl. Substitute both variable R groups by `*` to obtain `*OC(=O)C(/N=N\[N-]S(=O)(=O)c1cccc(C)c1)C(*)=O`.
